title: From repository behavior to review attention
description: A reconstructed stack of actual Docviz history: merged PRs #13, #14 and #15. These are historical layers, not currently open stacked GitHub PRs. No GitHub state is changed.

producer.name: Independent source reviewer
producer.scope: Independent examination of exact historical commits. Source interpretation only; no test, Jev or TLC execution is claimed.

summary: The cumulative change makes versioned repository behavior part of PR review. A model catalog supplies contracts and code-linked steps; the behavior layer produces comparison, rule and fidelity findings; the final layer turns those findings into explicit review attention and reasons.

layers.title: Give repository behavior a versioned home
layers.summary: Adds .atlas loading and validation: model files describe covered implementation, code-linked steps and checked rules. This layer makes behavior metadata readable from either the working directory or a Git revision; it does not run the models.

layers.behaviorBefore: The PR tooling has no helper/atlas.js loader and no repository .atlas model catalog at this target. PR diagrams and module movement already exist; behavior modeling itself is not being invented from nothing.
layers.behaviorAfter: Versioned model metadata, code membership, source-linked steps and rule names can be loaded and validated. Reading a model does not execute TLA or its view.
limitations: The bundled card-money model has no .atlas/rules.md in this snapshot; user-rule ownership is not established by the bundled invariants.
Coverage is declared by model code paths, not an exhaustive dependency or execution analysis.
No model execution, Jev check or behavioral correctness follows from successfully reading the catalog.

layers.behaviorBefore: Atlas metadata can be read, but the PR command does not yet run helper/behavior.js to compare model behavior and report its findings.
layers.behaviorAfter: PR review includes model runs, chart state/edge changes, rule outcomes, code-fidelity checks and coverage gaps. Failed or unavailable checks remain findings.
limitations: Model results concern the model and its configured bounds; source correspondence is separate.
The unit-test harness explicitly fakes TLC output. Parser/transformer execution against that data is real, but it is not a fresh model-checking result.
Jev is unavailable without TYPESAFE_API_KEY, so a live source judgment cannot be claimed.
Source coverage is a declared-path heuristic; it is not all runtime behavior or dependency coverage.

layers.title: Turn findings into review attention
layers.summary: Adds a deterministic ordered policy that combines PR-step and behavior findings into needs you, look when you can, or nothing for you. The verdict appears at the beginning of the generated PR comment.
layers.head: cb4e3ca60eec5d80cb94323fc7f35c65e32d0aa2

claims.label: A breaking modeled rule routes to needs you.
claims.condition: A rule or extra-rule finding has status breaks.
claims.expectation: The rule-breaks row assigns needs; the aggregate preserves that highest attention level and reason.

layers.behaviorBefore: Behavior findings are displayed, but this helper/verdict.js policy and aggregate attention headline do not exist.
layers.behaviorAfter: A PR gets one attention level plus ordered reasons derived from PR-step and behavior findings. This is routing based on supplied findings, not approval of the implementation.
limitations: verdict([]) returns nothing. An empty finding list does not prove a complete assessment; the application must keep coverage and completeness separate.
The policy can only classify findings supplied to it; missing observations are not automatically discovered here.
Controlled findings used in a replay are fixture inputs, not live Jev or TLC results.

edges.label: Supply model steps and source spans

composition.summary: Atlas identity and code membership feed both model comparison and source checks. Their findings meet at one attention policy; gaps in either producer must remain visible rather than being averaged away.
obligations: All layer summaries, source anchors and captures name their exact local base/head; the holistic scope is target to tip.
The output finding shape from behavior and PR source checking must remain compatible with verdict rows.
A code-fidelity score cannot stand in for a model run; a model result cannot establish implementation fidelity.
An empty or incomplete finding set cannot establish that the whole stack needs no review.
Real captured execution of parser/routing functions must identify mocked or controlled upstream inputs.
unverified: No fresh live Jev result is available.
No fresh TLC execution is established by this source review.
End-to-end provider execution and Chrome rendering are outside a controlled parser/routing replay.
